title: Movement preview dodges on the first frame of every fresh run
body:
## Summary
StickFigurePreview never resets timeRef, so after the first run every new run (Pause then Preview, or any tuning edit) schedules nextDodgeAt in the past and dodges immediately.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_character/playground/StickFigurePreview.tsx:80 sets nextDodgeAt = 2 + rand*2 for a fresh run (an absolute time), but t comes from timeRef.current (:87-88), which accumulates across every run and is never reset. After N seconds of play any fresh run has t >> nextDodgeAt, so the dodge branch (:104) fires on frame 1 and the figure jumps from posX=60 straight into a dodge; the preview no longer shows the acceleration ramp the user just tuned. Fixed: a fresh run rebases its schedule on the current t (nextDodgeAt = t + 2 + rand*2) or resets timeRef.

## Flow
- Press Preview, wait ~5 s, press Pause, press Preview
- fresh run: posX=60, nextDodgeAt in 2..4 s, t ~5 s
- frame 1 enters the dodge branch: ramp skipped
- Fix: extract the per-frame integrator as a pure step(state, dt) and rebase nextDodgeAt on t for fresh runs

## Expected impact
Designers tuning acceleration see the ramp instead of an instant dodge after every edit. Risk: the suspend/resume snapshot path (suspendable-raf.test) must keep restoring the same-key run unchanged.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the preview shows the tuned ramp before the first dodge on every run
Before: walked: a fresh run after 5 s of play dodges at frame 1 (t=5 > nextDodgeAt<=4)
After: predicted: first dodge >= 2 s into each fresh run
Method: simulation - three walked cases (first run, run after pause, run after a curve edit); the loop lives inside a canvas effect with no pure seam to drive from a test this round
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: extract step(state, dt) from the frame loop; test that a fresh run started at t=10 does not dodge in its first 1.9 s (red today)

title: Preview rAF loop restarts on every curve drag that does not change it
body:
## Summary
StickFigurePreview's effect depends on the whole values object, so dragging the camera curve (which the preview never reads) tears down and restarts the rAF loop on every pointermove.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_character/playground/StickFigurePreview.tsx:171 lists values in the deps beside the four derived factors and runKey; the body reads only the four factors. values is re-memoised in PlaygroundTab (decodeCurves(curves)) on every store write, so each pointermove on any curve runs cleanup (snapshot + cancelAnimationFrame) and setup again. The snapshot makes it visually lossless, but it is wasted work at pointermove rate. Fixed: drop values from the deps (runKey already encodes everything the loop reads).

## Flow
- Press Preview, drag a Camera Lag Response handle
- each pointermove -> store write -> new values object -> effect cleanup + restart
- Fix: deps = [isPlaying, speedFactor, accelFactor, dodgeDistFactor, dodgeDurFactor, runKey]

## Expected impact
Fewer effect teardowns while dragging; nothing user-visible changes. Risk: react-hooks/exhaustive-deps must stay clean (values is not read in the body).

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - zero loop restarts for drags on curves the preview does not read
Before: by inspection: 1 restart per camera-curve pointermove
After: predicted: 0
Method: simulation - counted from the dependency list; a cancelAnimationFrame spy over N simulated drags was not built this round
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_character/playground/StickFigurePreview.tsx:171 }, [isPlaying, speedFactor, accelFactor, dodgeDistFactor, dodgeDurFactor, values, runKey]);
instrument: render PlaygroundTab playing, spy cancelAnimationFrame, fire 10 camera-handle pointermoves; 10 today, 0 after

title: One-click Clear wipes every feel layer, including Playground and UE-adopted
body:
## Summary
FeelLayerStack's Clear button deletes the whole persisted layer stack with no confirmation or undo, including the reserved Playground curves and Adopted-from-UE layers.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_character/ai-feel/FeelLayerStack.tsx:73 onClick={clearFeelLayers}: a single click removes every layer from the persisted characterBlueprintStore, which the Playground tab and the UE drift panel also write (PLAYGROUND_LAYER_ID, UE_ADOPTED_LAYER_ID). The per-layer Remove (:164) is likewise immediate. The repo has a shared ui/ConfirmDialog for destructive actions. Fixed: confirm (naming how many layers, and that curve edits / UE adoptions go too), or a one-step undo.

## Flow
- Add two layers, drag a Playground curve, adopt one UE value
- AI Feel -> Adjustment Stack -> Clear
- all layers including curve edits and adoptions are gone, no way back

## Expected impact
Designers no longer lose a tuned stack to a misclick. Risk: FeelLayerStack.test asserts Clear empties the stack and would need the confirm step.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - destructive clear needs an explicit second step
Before: 1 click destroys N layers (N unbounded), 0 confirmations
After: 2 steps with the count named
Method: simulation - walked in the component; a test-first build was deferred because it changes interaction design
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: FeelLayerStack test: Clear with 3 layers leaves 3 until the confirm is accepted

title: Curve handles and state-machine nodes are pointer-only
body:
## Summary
CurveEditor's draggable handles and MovementStateMachine's nodes respond only to pointer/mouse events, so keyboard users cannot tune a curve or reveal transitions.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_character/playground/CurveEditor.tsx:151-166 handles are <circle> elements with onPointerDown only: no tabIndex, role, name or arrow-key nudge, so the Playground's core edit is unreachable without a pointer. src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_character/movement/MovementStateMachine.tsx:86-87 nodes highlight transitions on onMouseEnter/Leave only. Registry accessibility / primitive-level-a11y: keyboard operability and announced state are part of the control. Fixed: each handle a focusable role=slider (aria-valuenow/min/max/valuetext) with arrow-key nudges through the same onChange; nodes focusable with onFocus/onBlur mirroring hover.

## Flow
- Tab through the Playground: focus never lands on a curve handle
- Tab through Movement: no node takes focus; transition labels never show
- Fix: role=slider handles + arrow keys; focusable nodes

## Expected impact
Keyboard and AT users can edit feel curves. Risk: arrow nudges must respect the same neighbour X constraint as drag (CurveEditor.tsx:61-63).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - curve editing and transition reveal operable by keyboard
Before: 0 of 3 curve editors and 0 of 5 state nodes keyboard-operable
After: all operable
Method: simulation - counted from source; the slider build is M and was not taken this round
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_character/playground/CurveEditor.tsx:152 <circle cx={sp.x} cy={sp.y} r={12} fill="transparent" ... onPointerDown={handlePointerDown(i)} />
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_character/movement/MovementStateMachine.tsx:86 onMouseEnter={() => setHoveredState(i)}
instrument: render CurveEditor; getAllByRole("slider") length == draggable count; ArrowUp changes the onChange y (0 sliders today)

title: Sub-12px text in the movement SVG, curve axes and preview canvas
body:
## Summary
Seven ESLint legibility-floor warnings (8-9px SVG text) plus three unlinted 8-9px canvas fonts remain in this context.

## Description
ESLint (no-restricted-syntax legibility floor) warns at src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_character/movement/MovementStateMachine.tsx:112 (text-[9px] node labels) and src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_character/playground/CurveEditor.tsx:131,133 (9px axis labels) and :172 (8px tooltip): 7 warnings. Canvas text is invisible to the rule: src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_character/playground/canvas-draw.ts:108 '8px monospace', :113 'bold 9px monospace', src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_character/playground/StickFigurePreview.tsx:159 '9px monospace'. SVG text scales with the viewBox, so the rendered size depends on panel width; a fix must re-check label fit inside the NODE_RX=28 ellipses and the PAD.left=40 gutter.

## Flow
- npx eslint on movement/playground/ai-feel -> 7 legibility warnings
- Fix: TEXT_SCALE.meta (10px) or viewBox-aware sizing verified at the lg 3-column width; canvas fonts to 10px+

## Expected impact
Labels legible at the 10px meta tier. Risk: labels overflow ellipses or the curve gutter, so it needs a rendered check.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - zero legibility-floor warnings in the context
Before: 7 eslint warnings + 3 canvas sites
After: 0 + 0
Method: gate - the eslint count is measured; After was not taken because the visual fit needs a rendered screenshot this round may not run
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
npx eslint movement playground ai-feel -> 7 x no-restricted-syntax (legibility floor)
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_character/playground/canvas-draw.ts:108 ctx.font = '8px monospace';
instrument: eslint warning count (7 -> 0) plus one screenshot of Movement and Playground at lg width

title: A/B summary labels every Movement increase as "Faster"
body:
## Summary
ComparisonPanel counts any Movement field whose compare value is higher as "Faster" and lower as "Slower", including deceleration, air control, jump velocity and gravity scale.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_character/ai-feel/ComparisonPanel.tsx:85,90 filter c.category === 'Movement' && c.delta > 0 / < 0. Movement holds 8 fields in FEEL_FIELD_META (src/lib/character-feel-optimizer.ts:317-324): walk, sprint, acceleration, deceleration, turnRate, airControl, jumpZVelocity, gravityScale. A higher gravityScale or airControl is not "faster"; the copy asserts a meaning the data lacks, and its direction is B relative to A while the header reads A then B. Fixed: count only speed-like fields with the direction named ("<B> faster on N"), or relabel as Higher/Lower.

## Flow
- Compare Dark Souls Heavy against any preset with a higher gravityScale
- that field counts toward "Faster"

## Expected impact
The summary line means what it says. Risk: none beyond copy.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - summary counts match their label
Before: 4 of 8 Movement fields counted under a label that does not describe them
After: 0 of 8
Method: probe - read the field list against the filter; no test written this round
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: ComparisonPanel test over a fixture where only gravityScale rises: Faster must read 0 (1 today)

title: Movement tab acceleration curve ignores the feel stack the Playground edits
body:
## Summary
The Movement tab draws a fixed ACCEL_CURVE_POINTS curve while the Playground's acceleration curve is the resolved feel stack, so the two tabs show different acceleration for the same character.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_character/movement/MovementOverview.tsx:52 renders AccelCurve from _shared/data ACCEL_CURVE_POINTS/ACCEL_KEY_POINTS (static), whereas src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_character/playground/PlaygroundTab.tsx derives curves from resolveStack(preset.profile, feelLayers). Changing preset or dragging the accel curve changes nothing on the Movement tab. Related to the recorded motion-quality-gating deviation (hardcoded dodge stats) but a separate surface. Fixed: derive the Movement accel curve from the resolved profile (encodeCurves(resolved).accel), or label it a reference curve.

## Flow
- Playground: switch preset to Hades, drag the accel curve
- Movement tab: acceleration curve unchanged

## Expected impact
_shared/data is owned by character-overview-input; the edit stays in MovementOverview.tsx. Risk: AccelCurve expects cm/s points, the codec gives normalised points, so a mapping is needed.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - Movement tab acceleration follows the resolved stack
Before: 0 of 2 tabs agree after a preset change (walked)
After: 2 of 2
Method: simulation - walked through the two derivations; no render test built
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_character/movement/MovementOverview.tsx:52 <AccelCurve points={ACCEL_CURVE_POINTS} keyPoints={ACCEL_KEY_POINTS} .../>
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_character/playground/PlaygroundTab.tsx:260 const resolved = useMemo(() => resolveStack(preset.profile, feelLayers), [preset, feelLayers]);
instrument: render MovementOverview under two presets in the store; the curve path d must differ (identical today)

title: State-machine data is index-parallel to MOVEMENT_STATES; Sprint cannot dodge
body:
## Summary
state-machine-data.ts positions and transitions address MOVEMENT_STATES by array index with no guard, MovementStateMachine hardcodes index 4 as Dodge, and the graph has no Sprint->Dodge edge though Idle/Walk/Run->Dodge exist.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_character/movement/state-machine-data.ts:1-7 STATE_POSITIONS is a positional list commented Idle..Dodge; :10-21 STATE_TRANSITIONS use numeric from/to. MOVEMENT_STATES lives in src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_character/_shared/data.ts:155 (owned by character-overview-input). src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_character/movement/MovementStateMachine.tsx:128 colours the Dodge note with MOVEMENT_STATES[4] and the Sprint note with ACCENT_ORANGE directly. A reorder or insert in MOVEMENT_STATES silently mis-wires the graph. Separately, from 3 (Sprint) to 4 (Dodge) is absent: either a data gap or a gameplay rule that should be stated; the UE dodge gating decides which.

## Flow
- Insert a Crouch state into MOVEMENT_STATES at index 2
- graph draws Run edges to Crouch and the Dodge note takes the wrong colour
- Fix: key positions/transitions by label; add a guard test; resolve Sprint->Dodge against UE

## Expected impact
The diagram cannot drift from the state list. Risk: needs a label key or a local label map.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - state graph derived from / guarded against the state list
Before: 0 guards; 1 hardcoded index; 3 of 4 locomotion states reach Dodge
After: 1 guard; 0 hardcoded indices; Sprint edge present or documented
Method: simulation - walked the insert case; the Sprint->Dodge truth needs the UE source
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_character/movement/state-machine-data.ts:17-19 { from: 0, to: 4 }, { from: 1, to: 4 }, { from: 2, to: 4 }  (no from: 3)
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_character/movement/MovementStateMachine.tsx:128 MOVEMENT_STATES[4].color
instrument: guard test: STATE_POSITIONS.length === MOVEMENT_STATES.length and every transition index in range; grep ARPGCharacterBase dodge gating for sprint
